title: userFilters on an object list view is silently dropped — warn until the ADR-0053 phase-4 guardrail lands
body:
## Context

Per ADR-0053 (`docs/adr/0053-list-view-navigation-modes.md`), an object's default list (`ObjectView`, "views" mode) has exactly one nav control — the `ViewTabBar` — and `userFilters` belongs to page lists (`InterfaceListPage`, "filters" mode) only. Phase 1 (suppress in-list rows) landed in PR #1801:

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:1299-1304` — `renderListView` hardcodes `quickFilters: undefined, userFilters: undefined`.

That suppression is correct. The problem is that it is **completely silent**, and the phase-4 guardrail that was supposed to catch the wrong-context authoring error never landed:

- `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:287` — `userFilters: UserFiltersSchema.optional()` is accepted on the list-view schema with no context `refine`, no `check`/`doctor` rule.

So an author (human or AI) who writes `userFilters` on an object list view gets a schema that validates, a build that passes, and a page that renders **nothing** where they expect filter dropdowns — zero signal at any layer. Found while dogfooding `app-showcase` (its `showcase_task.tabular` view carries exactly this wrong-context block, with a stale ADR-0047 comment).

## Ask

Until the full phase-4 guardrail (zod `refine` + `check` rule) is implemented:

- In `ObjectView.tsx` `renderListView`, when the incoming view def / list schema actually carries `userFilters` (or `quickFilters`), emit a `console.warn` explaining that the field is ignored in views mode and belongs to page lists — same "never swallow silently" treatment as #2217.

Phase 4 proper (schema-level rejection) can then supersede the warning.
